title: upgrade-attention-kernels-rope-rotary-fused-flash-variants
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce token latency and increase throughput for medium-to-long context workloads by shipping a new set of attention kernels and a couple runtime scheduling tweaks. This PR introduces two FlashAttention variants (memory-optimized and fused-qkv path), a fused rotary/rope pre-rotation step, and scheduler-side heuristics that improve continuous batching and KV cache locality. It also contains microbenchmarks, CI hooks, and a migration note for custom kernel fallbacks. Changes include kernel sources, host-side glue, scheduler policy, and perf harnesses. Checklist: [x] flash variants implemented and unit-tested [x] fused qkv and rotary op added [x] continuous batcher heuristics updated [x] KV prefix cache integration with kernel fast-path [x] benchmarks added [x] documentation and migration notes added. Summary of changes and rationale: we observed recurring tail latency spikes for long conversations due to inefficient rotary application and extra memory copies in QKV paths. The memory-optimized Flash variant reduces intermediate allocations by streaming rotary application into fused matmul kernels. The fused-qkv path removes a roundtrip copy for QKV interleaving when model layout is compatible. Scheduler improvements bias batch formation to keep high prefix-reuse requests together and to avoid splitting high-KV-hit requests across GPU lanes. This reduces KV cache churn and improves effective throughput for chat workloads. Compatibility: kernels have runtime probes and fall back to previous CUDA kernels if compute capability or workspace is incompatible. Documentation in docs/perf/attn-kernels.md explains runtime flags and a new REDWOOD_ATTN_KERNEL env var for operators. Testing and benching: microbench harness (benchmarks/attn_latency.yaml) reproduces production-like distributions (50/30/20 split for small/medium/long contexts). End-to-end perf runs were executed on dedicated CI runners with A100/80GB and RTX6000 pools. Observed improvements (median across 5 runs): - LLaMA-2-13B, seq=512: p50 latency down 27% (from 112ms to 82ms), throughput up 1.8x for streaming-batched workloads. - Llama-2-7B, seq=2048: p95 latency down 34% and 2.1x throughput in high-KV-reuse scenarios due to reduced cache churn. - Memory working set reduced by ~18% on average for long-context workloads. Runtime regression guard: perf-evals are included in CI and a canary rollout config is added in the console so we can route 5% traffic to the new kernels for a week before full rollout. Rollout plan included. Migration notes: customers with custom CUDA kernels should set REDWOOD_ATTN_KERNEL=legacy to disable new paths. Related: SUP-4412 (support ticket with a customer workload that motivated isolated KV churn investigation).
